summary: Keystore rollover triggered SIGABRT chain in runtime leading to elevated 5xx rate in prod us-east
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled keystore rotation in prod us-east on 2026-03-13 15:40 UTC, we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the API gateway. Investigation indicates multiple downstream serving runtime processes terminated with SIGABRT shortly after the keystore swap, causing elevated error rate and client request failures.

Impact:
- ~12% error rate increase across affected routes for ~18 minutes.
- Several enterprise customers (including AcmeCloud) reported failed streaming and generation requests.
- Automated retries caused additional load and exacerbated upstream failures.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- API Gateway version: apigw-v2.14.1
- Serving runtime: runtime-v1.86 (NVIDIA accel nodes)
- Keystore service: vault-rotator-v0.9

Observed behavior:
- Keystore rotation completed at 15:40 UTC. 15:41:10 UTC first SIGABRT observed in runtime-worker-12. Within 2 minutes 8 runtime workers crashed in rapid succession. API Gateway began returning 502/503s and 504s for in-flight requests.
- Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/streams. Non-streaming small-embed endpoints saw degradation but less severe.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back keystore to previous version (15:48 UTC) and paused automated rotations.
- Temporarily increased graceful restart window on serving runtime to avoid simultaneous process exit.
- Put affected customers on dedicated fallback routes to minimize impact while we investigate.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger keystore rotation in prod-us-east using vault-rotator staged rollout (canary=false).
2) Observe serving runtime worker processes during rotation with process supervision logging enabled.
3) Note sudden SIGABRTs in runtimes with stack traces referencing libcrypto and keystore client handshake code.
4) API Gateway /v1/generate starts returning 502/503 within first 90s of rotation if multiple runtimes restart concurrently.
logs: Runtime worker crash excerpt: runtime-worker-12 SIGABRT at 2026-03-13T15:41:10Z. Backtrace points at keystore_client.cc:142 (openssl HSM lookup).
APIGW logs: 502 spikes start 15:41:20 UTC, peak at 15:45 UTC (~18% 5xx across routes).
Vault-rotator log: rotation-step completed 15:40:02 UTC; post-rotate key-publish ack from 3 of 5 nodes.
timeline: 2026-03-13T15:41:10Z - runtime-worker-12 SIGABRT observed. First 502s reported to SRE alerting.
2026-03-13T15:42:00Z - Multiple runtime workers crash; API gateway error rate climbs.
2026-03-13T15:48:30Z - Rollback of keystore performed; rotation paused globally.
2026-03-13T16:02:00Z - Error rate returns to baseline after progressive runtime restarts and circuit breakers adjust.
comments: Aisha Nguyen (Reporter) - 2026-03-13T15:47:00Z: Customer AcmeCloud reported repeated failures on streaming endpoint. Escalating to SRE and runtime oncall.
Ben Carter (Assignee) - 2026-03-13T15:50:00Z: Paused keystore rotations account-wide and initiated rollback. Gathering runtime logs and core dumps.
SRE-Triage (Slack #incidents) - 2026-03-13T15:55:00Z: Observed SIGABRTs with OpenSSL stack; possible HSM/keystore client incompatibility after key refresh.
RuntimeEng (Slack #runtime) - 2026-03-13T16:05:00Z: Reproduced crash locally with simulated keystore key swap when multiple worker threads request TLS identity simultaneously.
Ben Carter - 2026-03-13T16:20:00Z: Temporary mitigation applied: staggered worker restart window and increased backoff on keystore client retries.
investigation: Hypothesis 1: New key material published during rotation triggered a race in keystore client leading to double-free in OpenSSL wrappers when multiple threads load identities concurrently.
Hypothesis 2: Partial ack from keystore cluster (3/5 nodes) caused transient cert validation failures; in combination with aggressive client retry, produced invalid memory state.
Test run: Replayed rotation in staging with 50 parallel streaming clients; core dump reproduced reliably when rotation applied without staggered worker restarts.
Captured core dumps and ran addr2line; crash frames map to keystore_client::refresh_identities -> OpenSSL EVP_PKEY_free.
root_cause: A race in the keystore client code path that manages in-memory identity refresh during key rotation. When multiple runtime worker threads concurrently refreshed identities after a rotation, a use-after-free/double-free in the OpenSSL wrapper was triggered, resulting in SIGABRTs and cascading 5xx responses from API Gateway.
resolution: Short-term: Rolled back rotation and paused automated rotations until a code fix is deployed. Staggered restart windows added to runtime supervisor to avoid synchronized refreshes.
Medium-term: Patch submitted to keystore client to add thread-safe identity swap (PR: github.com/redwood/serving/PR-7605).
Long-term: Add pre-rotation canary that performs identity refresh on a single worker cluster before full rollout; include HSM ack threshold verification step.
follow_up: Action: Backport keystore client thread-safety patch to runtime-stable branch. Owner: RuntimeEng (PR-7605). Due: 2026-03-17

Action: Communication: Customer impact notice sent to affected enterprise customers; schedule postmortem with AcmeCloud. Owner: CS. Due: 2026-03-16
Action: Add automated test in CI to simulate concurrent identity refresh under load. Owner: Infra QA. Due: 2026-03-20
